note: Volume I, Number 11. The school for young ladies is named and dated — its proprietor proposes it, its fall term opens Monday 17 August, and enquiries go to Henry Moore's office. The tailor is named too, Edward Burton, and his street reads LAKE here, which is what withdrew the Franklin Street reading 1835-07-25 had recorded. A. Garrett reappears as an auctioneer at No. 1 Dearborn street, and Frederick Thomas's patent medicine shelf is set out brand by brand.

claims.notes: THE SCHOOL HAS A NAME AND A DATE: a school FOR YOUNG LADIES proposed by someone named HUNT, opening its fall term on Monday 17 August 1835 and becoming permanent only if enough subscribers come forward. Enquiries go 'at the office of Henry [Moore]' — the attorney whose own office this run places in J. H. Kinzie's new store and who is secretary of the Chicago Reading Room. So one lawyer's office is the town's clearing house for its two new civic ventures, which is a real fact about how a town of 3,000 organised itself. THE TITLE AND FORENAME ARE DESTROYED: 'Me RK {ABLES HUNT' could be Mrs., Miss or Mr. and a forename, and the difference decides whether the proprietor of a girls' school was a woman — which is exactly the sort of thing that must not be guessed. The surname alone is minted. Greek joins Latin and French in this printing's fee scale.

business.name: a new tailoring establishment, Chicago, June 1835

claims.notes: THE TAILOR IS EDWARD BURTON, late of New York — a forename only in the three earlier printings. HIS STREET IS STILL NOT SETTLED AND THIS PRINTING IS WHY. 1835-06-27 reads 'Shop in Frank eter street'; 1835-07-25 reads 'a Bhop ia rroklia', which that claim took as FRANKLIN; 1835-08-01 reads 'Shop in Laks runlie'; and this one reads 'having taken a [shop in] lake - street' with the word clean. Two witnesses for Lake, one for Franklin, one unreadable — so the 07-25 claim's Franklin Street inference has been WITHDRAWN from the business (the reading itself still stands in that file's quote) and no street is recorded here either. A page-image pass decides it. A. GARRETT, whose South Water Street store Montgomery took over in July, is here signing as an auctioneer in his own right at No. 1 Dearborn street — a street number, which is the only one in the entire run.

business.name: Frederick Thomas, drugs and paints
business.trade: drugs, paints, chemicals, perfumery and dye stuffs

claims.notes: THE PATENT MEDICINE SHELF, BRAND BY BRAND — Turlington's Balsam, Lee's Pills, an elixir of life, a preserving cordial, a carminative balm, an anti-bilious and inflammatory specific and an anti-consumptive. Set beside Russell & Clift's Evans's Hygeian agency, the London and Paris Hygeian pills, Dr. Buchan's acoustic oil and Frederick Thomas's own Fire King's cholera specific, the run now documents a substantial patent-medicine trade in a town of under three thousand people. Thomas is also still restocking by lake — 'part of his [supplies in] Drugs, Paints, Perfumery, Oils and Dye Stuffs have been received', the same sentence 1835-07-04 carried with the schooner named and cut.

claims.notes: BROWN THE PAINTER IS STILL OVER BRIGGS & HUMPHREY'S in mid-August, ten weeks after his first insertion — the anchor is legible here and the street word is not, so Randolph Street is carried from the 1835-06-13 printing where both were. An upper-floor tenancy holding for a whole summer is worth more than a single notice: it says Briggs & Humphrey's building had a let floor over it as a standing arrangement. THREE ADVERTISEMENTS ARE QUOTED TOGETHER because the segmenter runs them into one line, and the other two are both corroborations rather than new claims: Montgomery's two auction stores, and Frederick Thomas's Water Street drug store under its full sign, 'NEW DRUG, MEDICINE, PAINT AND OIL STORE'.
